claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children. Let me start with a few questions.

**First, how many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my child - just the one. Their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! That's helpful. So I'm assessing eligibility for Alex.

Let me start by gathering the key information I need. 

**How old is Alex, or what is their date of birth?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to understand Alex's current situation a bit better.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. They're doing their A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I need to confirm a few more details about Alex's living situation.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more important questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you a British citizen, European Economic Area (EEA) citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Let me ask this more specifically to ensure I have the right information for the eligibility assessment.

**What is your immigration status? Are you a British citizen, an EEA citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh right, yes - I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. I have just one more question to complete my assessment.

**Are you currently receiving any other UK social security benefits, such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the rules carefully.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules, I'm pleased to inform you of the outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex's age and education:** Even though Alex is 19, they still qualify for Child Benefit because they're in full-time approved education (A-levels). Child Benefit continues until age 20 for children in approved education or training.

- **Living arrangements:** Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for their care.

- **Your eligibility:** You're a British citizen living in the UK, which meets the residency and citizenship requirements.

- **No benefit barriers:** You're not receiving other benefits that would restrict your eligibility.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can apply through HMRC (Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs). If you have any other questions or circumstances change, feel free to contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
